p16.role: England all-type A&E attendances, including UTCs, MIUs and walk-in centres, in the 2024-25 annual period

a1.role: September 2026 all-type A&E attendance relative to the 2024-25 average monthly attendance

methods.rationale: Uses the annual all-type total as the scale anchor, converts it to an average month, and applies a seasonal-and-trend factor for September 2026. This is the broadest historical baseline. Main failure mode is that p16 is for 2024-25 and its reporting scope may differ slightly from 2026; a1 carries the trend and September seasonality. Shared dependency with m2 and m3 on the same NHS England A&E collection.

p20.role: England all-type A&E attendances in April 2026

a2.role: September 2026 all-type A&E attendance relative to April 2026

methods.rationale: Anchors directly on the observed April 2026 all-type monthly total and applies a September/April ratio. This uses the most recent complete spring month in the evidence. Main failure mode is that September seasonality and any summer/autumn demand change are captured only by a2; a reporting-scope change would bias both numerator and baseline. Correlated with m1 and m3 through the same NHS England collection.

p72.role: England all-type A&E attendances in May 2026, a record month

a3.role: September 2026 all-type A&E attendance relative to May 2026

methods.rationale: Anchors on the May 2026 record monthly total and applies a September/May ratio. This tests whether the high 2026 demand level persists into September. Main failure mode is that May may be an anomalous peak and September could be materially lower; a3 is deliberately wide. It is not independent of m2 because both use recent months from the same collection.

a4.role: September 2026 emergency admissions relative to April 2026

a5.role: September 2026 A&E attendances per emergency admission

methods.rationale: Uses emergency admissions as an independent flow measure: April 2026 admissions are adjusted to September and multiplied by attendances per admission. This is a cross-check on the attendance-based routes rather than a primary method. Main failure modes are a shift in admission thresholds, case mix, or the conversion rate; a4 and a5 carry those uncertainties. Shared monthly release with the attendance totals, so it is not fully independent of reporting changes.

assumptions.name: September 2026 attendance relative to 2024-25 average monthly attendance
assumptions.rationale: p16 gives the 2024-25 annual all-type total. Recent 2026 months in p20 and p72 indicate elevated demand relative to that annual average, while September is usually not the highest month. A modest upward factor is appropriate, with a range covering weaker or stronger seasonality and growth.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 has similar reporting scope and broadly similar seasonality/growth to the recent 2026 months observed before the cutoff.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published September 2025 or September 2026 total far outside the implied range, or evidence of a material reporting-scope change.

assumptions.name: September 2026 attendance relative to April 2026
assumptions.rationale: p20 gives the actual April 2026 all-type total. The May record in p72 and the near-record March level implied by p73 show recent demand is at least as high as April; September is set slightly above April but with a wide range because no September monthly history is available.
assumptions.applies_when: The September/April seasonal relationship is roughly stable and no major respiratory or reporting shock occurs between April and September 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published September 2025 monthly total or early September 2026 partial data showing a markedly different September/April ratio.

assumptions.name: September 2026 attendance relative to May 2026
assumptions.rationale: p72 shows May 2026 was a record month. September is usually below a spring record peak, but the range allows September to remain near or above May if demand stays elevated.
assumptions.applies_when: The May 2026 record reflects demand levels that transfer, with normal seasonality, into September 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that May 2026 was an anomalous reporting month, or September 2025/2026 data showing a very different September/May ratio.

assumptions.name: September 2026 emergency admissions relative to April 2026
assumptions.rationale: p66 gives April 2026 emergency admissions. Admissions often rise into autumn and winter, so a small increase over April is plausible; the range covers flat to moderate growth.
assumptions.applies_when: Emergency admissions in September 2026 follow the usual autumn pattern and there is no major change in admission thresholds.
assumptions.falsified_by: Published September 2025/2026 emergency admissions showing a materially different September/April ratio.

assumptions.name: September 2026 A&E attendances per emergency admission
assumptions.rationale: The April 2026 emergency admissions in p66 and the April 2026 attendances in p20 imply about 4.46 attendances per emergency admission. This is used as a conversion factor for September, allowing for drift in case mix and admission thresholds.
assumptions.applies_when: The A&E attendance-to-emergency-admission conversion rate remains broadly similar to the April 2026 ratio.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published September conversion rate outside the stated range, or a sharp change in emergency admission thresholds or A&E case mix.

assumptions.name: September 2026 seasonal factor relative to average monthly attendance in 2026-27
assumptions.rationale: p16 gives the 2024-25 annual all-type total and p21 gives recent total year-on-year growth; applying that growth over the roughly two years to September 2026 and using a September seasonal factor near the annual average bridges the annual total to the target. p20 and p72 show 2026 months above the 2024-25 monthly average, but September is not usually the peak month.
assumptions.applies_when: Recent total growth embedded in p21 persists through 2026-27 and September is near the annual monthly average.
assumptions.falsified_by: September 2026 daily returns or a reporting change show attendance far from the annual average or growth materially away from p21.

assumptions.name: September 2026 attendance relative to April 2026
assumptions.rationale: p20 is the April 2026 all-type total. p72 and p73 show May 2026 was a record, and p21 shows positive April year-on-year growth. September is often close to April in level but can be lower, so the ratio is centered near parity with a wide range for weekday composition and seasonality.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 has a similar weekday and seasonal pattern to April 2026 and no major reporting-scope change.
assumptions.falsified_by: September 2026 totals deviate materially from April after adjusting for weekday composition.

assumptions.name: September 2026 attendance relative to May 2026
assumptions.rationale: p72 is the record May 2026 total. May is typically a high month and September is usually lower, while p20 and p21 indicate a high underlying 2026 level. The ratio is therefore below one but not deeply so.
assumptions.applies_when: May 2026 is a valid high-season anchor and September follows the usual May-to-September decline.
assumptions.falsified_by: September 2026 is at or above the May record, or May was distorted by a one-off reporting change.

assumptions.name: September 2026 emergency admissions relative to April 2026
assumptions.rationale: p66 gives April 2026 emergency admissions. Emergency admissions are seasonal and September is usually similar to or slightly below April, while p21 shows positive underlying A&E growth. The range covers respiratory and weather uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: Emergency admissions in September 2026 follow usual April-to-September seasonality.
assumptions.falsified_by: September admissions surge or fall outside the range because of respiratory, weather, or reporting shocks.

assumptions.name: September 2026 attendances per emergency admission relative to April 2026
assumptions.rationale: p20 and p66 jointly determine the April 2026 attendances-per-emergency-admission conversion. September case mix is assumed to leave that conversion near April after allowing for Type 1 and Type 3 growth differences in p22, p23, p61, and p62.
assumptions.applies_when: The admissions-to-attendance conversion remains near the April 2026 level after case-mix adjustment.
assumptions.falsified_by: Type 1/Type 3 case mix or admission thresholds shift materially.

assumptions.name: Type 1 September 2026 attendance relative to April 2026
assumptions.rationale: p68 and p32 recover the April 2026 Type 1 total, and p22 and p61 show recent Type 1 growth. September is assumed to be near April for Type 1, with uncertainty from seasonality and reporting scope.
assumptions.applies_when: Type 1 September attendance follows usual seasonality relative to April and recent growth persists.
assumptions.falsified_by: Type 1 growth diverges from p22/p61 or reporting scope changes.

assumptions.name: Type 3 September 2026 attendance relative to April 2026
assumptions.rationale: p69 and p33 recover the April 2026 Type 3 total, and p23 and p62 show Type 3 growth was positive but weaker than Type 1. Type 3 services are assumed to move slightly above April, with a range covering MIU/WIC reporting changes.
assumptions.applies_when: Type 3 September attendance follows usual seasonality relative to April and recent growth persists.
assumptions.falsified_by: Type 3 growth diverges from p23/p62 or MIU/WIC reporting changes.

assumptions.name: Other A&E types September 2026 attendance relative to April 2026
assumptions.rationale: The other-type component is the residual after subtracting type-recovered Type 1 and Type 3 from p20. It is small and has less direct evidence, so the change factor is centered at parity with a wide range for reclassification.
assumptions.applies_when: The small residual other-type group moves roughly with the April-to-September average.
assumptions.falsified_by: A provider reclassification shifts material volume into or out of other types.

methods.label: m1

p16.role: England all-type A&E attendances, including UTCs, MIUs and walk-in centres, in the 2024-25 annual period

p21.role: England total A&E attendance year-on-year growth, April 2026 vs April 2025, used as the recent annual total-growth proxy

a1.role: September 2026 seasonal factor relative to average monthly attendance in 2026-27

methods.rationale: Reuses the annual 2024-25 all-type total and applies recent total growth from p21 over the roughly two years to September 2026, then a dimensionless September seasonal factor. Shared dependency: p21 is an April year-on-year growth rate, not a full annual series; if 2026 growth differs materially, m1 biases. Failure mode: annual average and September seasonality do not match the recent monthly patt

methods.label: m2

p20.role: England all-type A&E attendances in April 2026

a2.role: September 2026 all-type A&E attendance relative to April 2026

methods.rationale: Directly projects the April 2026 all-type total to September using a September/April seasonal ratio. It is anchored on an observed 2026 all-type month and avoids annual-average assumptions. Main failure modes: April was atypical, or September 2026 has an unusual weekday or reporting composition.

methods.label: m3

p72.role: England all-type A&E attendances in May 2026, a record month

a3.role: September 2026 all-type A&E attendance relative to May 2026

methods.rationale: Projects the record May 2026 total to September using a below-one May-to-September ratio. It uses the most recent high 2026 monthly total. Main failure modes: May was a one-off record or September departs from the usual post-May decline.

methods.label: m4

p20.role: England all-type A&E attendances in April 2026

a4.role: September 2026 emergency admissions relative to April 2026

a6.role: September 2026 attendances per emergency admission relative to April 2026

methods.rationale: Admissions-based route: April emergency admissions are moved to September by an admissions seasonal factor, and the April conversion is recovered from p20/p66 and adjusted by a September conversion factor. Shared dependency with p20 means it is not fully independent of the attendance routes. Failure mode: admission thresholds or case mix change the conversion.

methods.rationale: Department-type sum: Type 1 and Type 3 April totals are recovered from within-4-hour counts and shares, the residual other-type group is obtained from p20, and each component is projected to September. This uses type-level evidence and allows Type 1 and Type 3 to move differently. Shared dependency: p32/p33 and p68/p69 are same-source and not independent of p20; failure mode: within-4-hour shares

kept.name: September 2026 seasonal factor relative to average monthly attendance in 2026-27
kept.rationale: p16 gives the 2024-25 annual all-type total and p21 gives recent total year-on-year growth; applying that growth over the roughly two years to September 2026 and using a September seasonal factor near the annual average bridges the annual total to the target. p20 and p72 show 2026 months above the 2
kept.applies_when: Recent total growth embedded in p21 persists through 2026-27 and September is near the annual monthly average.
kept.falsified_by: September 2026 daily returns or a reporting change show attendance far from the annual average or growth materially away from p21.

kept.name: September 2026 attendance relative to April 2026
kept.rationale: p20 is the April 2026 all-type total. p72 and p73 show May 2026 was a record, and p21 shows positive April year-on-year growth. September is often close to April in level but can be lower, so the ratio is centered near parity with a wide range for weekday composition and seasonality.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 has a similar weekday and seasonal pattern to April 2026 and no major reporting-scope change.
kept.falsified_by: September 2026 totals deviate materially from April after adjusting for weekday composition.

kept.name: September 2026 attendance relative to May 2026
kept.rationale: p72 is the record May 2026 total. May is typically a high month and September is usually lower, while p20 and p21 indicate a high underlying 2026 level. The ratio is therefore below one but not deeply so.
kept.applies_when: May 2026 is a valid high-season anchor and September follows the usual May-to-September decline.
kept.falsified_by: September 2026 is at or above the May record, or May was distorted by a one-off reporting change.

kept.name: September 2026 emergency admissions relative to April 2026
kept.rationale: p66 gives April 2026 emergency admissions. Emergency admissions are seasonal and September is usually similar to or slightly below April, while p21 shows positive underlying A&E growth. The range covers respiratory and weather uncertainty.
kept.applies_when: Emergency admissions in September 2026 follow usual April-to-September seasonality.
kept.falsified_by: September admissions surge or fall outside the range because of respiratory, weather, or reporting shocks.

kept.name: September 2026 attendances per emergency admission relative to April 2026
kept.rationale: p20 and p66 jointly determine the April 2026 attendances-per-emergency-admission conversion. September case mix is assumed to leave that conversion near April after allowing for Type 1 and Type 3 growth differences in p22, p23, p61, and p62.
kept.applies_when: The admissions-to-attendance conversion remains near the April 2026 level after case-mix adjustment.
kept.falsified_by: Type 1/Type 3 case mix or admission thresholds shift materially.

kept.name: Type 1 September 2026 attendance relative to April 2026
kept.rationale: p68 and p32 recover the April 2026 Type 1 total, and p22 and p61 show recent Type 1 growth. September is assumed to be near April for Type 1, with uncertainty from seasonality and reporting scope.
kept.applies_when: Type 1 September attendance follows usual seasonality relative to April and recent growth persists.
kept.falsified_by: Type 1 growth diverges from p22/p61 or reporting scope changes.

kept.name: Type 3 September 2026 attendance relative to April 2026
kept.rationale: p69 and p33 recover the April 2026 Type 3 total, and p23 and p62 show Type 3 growth was positive but weaker than Type 1. Type 3 services are assumed to move slightly above April, with a range covering MIU/WIC reporting changes.
kept.applies_when: Type 3 September attendance follows usual seasonality relative to April and recent growth persists.
kept.falsified_by: Type 3 growth diverges from p23/p62 or MIU/WIC reporting changes.

kept.name: Other A&E types September 2026 attendance relative to April 2026
kept.rationale: The other-type component is the residual after subtracting type-recovered Type 1 and Type 3 from p20. It is small and has less direct evidence, so the change factor is centered at parity with a wide range for reclassification.
kept.applies_when: The small residual other-type group moves roughly with the April-to-September average.
kept.falsified_by: A provider reclassification shifts material volume into or out of other types.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
